items.title: Student of Desire
items.description:
It’s one thing to think abstractly about what men want, as a literary or philosophical question, or even to decry sexism as a social phenomenon; it’s another to be a single woman in New York City seeking love and partnership, and to worry that what you have to offer is not especially desired by those you are attracted to. 
 The post  Student of Desire  appeared first on  The Point Magazine .

items.title: Internal Goods
items.description:
I would like to reflect on the responsibilities of academics like myself in cases like this one, and to suggest that, if we hope to sustain human bonds or a world of shared value, clear thinking is the only way to do so. 
 The post  Internal Goods  appeared first on  The Point Magazine .

items.title: My Lavender Marriage
items.description:
I started seeing “MY HUSBAND IS GAY!” videos in the early 2020s when my TikTok algorithm, with its typical eerie prescience, decided to remind me that I was in a lavender marriage. 
 The post  My Lavender Marriage  appeared first on  The Point Magazine .

items.title: On Radical Preservation
items.description:
Our contention is that, if we fail to think through and delimit the role of AI in our lives, we risk undermining the intelligibility of our own guiding cultural concepts, and thus initiating a period in our own society of which it may someday be possible to say that “nothing happened.” 
 The post  On Radical Preservation  appeared first on  The Point Magazine .

items.title: Getting Good
items.description:

 The post  Getting Good  appeared first on  The Point Magazine .

items.title: After the Post-Avant-Garde
items.description:
When the art market can get by with flashy and ineffectual figurative paintings that are easy to sell on Instagram, it no longer has any reason to care about what’s going on in artistic subcultures. Indeed, those subcultures no longer have any reason to care about themselves. 
 The post  After the Post-Avant-Garde  appeared first on  The Point Magazine .

items.title: After the Sublime
items.description:
The problem with  Backrooms —like much of the online content that inspired it—is less that it relies too much on vibe and more that it fails to understand what makes that vibe interesting in the first place. 
 The post  After the Sublime  appeared first on  The Point Magazine .

items.title: We Were the 99 Percent
items.description:
As the global tides have continued to shift rightward, I’ve found myself going back to those initial days of Occupy, looking for clues. What was it about the movement that captured the imagination of an entire generation? 
 The post  We Were the 99 Percent  appeared first on  The Point Magazine .

items.title: Girls Wrestling
items.description:
